statement: Paused Free projects can be restored from the dashboard for 90 days.

evidence.quote: ![Project Paused: 90 Days Remaining](https://supabase.com/docs/img/guides/platform/paused-90-day.png)
When a project is paused, users have a 1-year window to restore the project on the platform from within Supabase Studio.

expected: Superseded: the restore window is 1 year. The 90-day figure survives only in an old screenshot's caption on the same page.

statement: PrivateLink keeps all Supabase traffic, including the Data API, Auth, Storage and Realtime, off the public internet.

evidence.quote: It does not support other Supabase services like API, Storage, Auth, or Realtime.
keeps your database traffic within the AWS network backbone.

expected: Corrected: PrivateLink covers direct database (5432) and pooler (6543) connections only. API, Storage, Auth and Realtime still go over the public internet.

statement: Every Team or Enterprise project is HIPAA compliant out of the box and can store PHI.

evidence.quote: Organizations must have a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with Supabase and have the HIPAA add-on enabled when dealing with Protected Health Information (PHI).
When the HIPAA add-on is enabled on an organization, projects within the organization can be configured as *High Compliance*.

expected: Corrected: PHI needs a signed BAA, the paid HIPAA add-on and projects configured as High Compliance (PITR, SSL enforcement, network restrictions, connection logging). Being on the Team plan is a precondition, not compliance.

statement: Any Supabase customer, on any plan, can download the SOC 2 Type 2 report.

evidence.quote: To access the SOC 2 Type 2 report, you must be a Enterprise or Team Plan Supabase customer.

expected: Corrected: the SOC 2 Type 2 report is for Team and Enterprise customers only.

statement: Choosing the Europe region keeps the primary database, Auth and Storage inside the EU.

evidence.quote: For example, the "Europe" general region includes London and Zurich, which are not EU member states.
If your compliance requirements call for data to stay within the EU specifically, choose a specific EU region rather than the general Europe grouping.

expected: Corrected: the Europe general region can land in London or Zurich. EU-only residency needs a specific EU region such as eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-3 or eu-north-1.

statement: Supabase runs a paid bug bounty on HackerOne.

evidence.quote: The program is currently recognition-only. Paid bounties will launch in 2026, scaled by severity and impact.

expected: Said as planned: the HackerOne program is a recognition-only VDP. Paid bounties were announced for 2026, and no d1 source confirms they launched.

statement: Supabase blocks commits containing secret keys before they reach GitHub (push protection).

evidence.quote: We're working with GitHub to add push protection, which will block commits containing secret keys before they reach the repository.

expected: Said as planned: today leaked keys are detected after commit through GitHub secret scanning and revoked; push protection is being worked on.

statement: Enterprise customers can deploy Supabase into their own cloud account (Bring Your Own Cloud).

evidence.quote: Bring Your Own Cloud will be available to more customers beyond Supabase for Platforms.

expected: Said as planned: BYOC was listed under 2026 plans as coming to more customers beyond Supabase for Platforms. It is not a general Enterprise option in the sources.

statement: Every database connection is logged by default (marked Current, last reviewed 2025-03-10).

evidence.quote: No. Supabase sets Postgres `log_connections` to off by default for new projects.
If your SOC 2 program requires connection audit evidence, enable connection logging and define how you retain and review those logs.

expected: Caught as past review and wrong: connection logging is off by default for new projects. HIPAA and high-compliance projects must turn it on, and the Security Advisor warns if it is off. The entry also confuses Supabase's own staff-activity audit logs with customer database logs.

statement: One entry says PITR restores to the minute; the other says to seconds of granularity.

evidence.quote: to roll back to any specific point in time, down to the minute
giving you the option to restore to any chosen point with up to seconds of granularity.

expected: Flagged as a conflict between the billing page and the backups guide. The backups guide, the product's own page and newer (2026-11-12), wins: up to seconds of granularity.

statement: One entry says all data stays in the chosen region; the other says backups, logs, exports, Edge Function execution and sub-processors can affect residency.

evidence.quote: All data will remain within the chosen region.
Backups, logs, data exported to external systems, Edge Function execution, and sub-processors can affect your data residency and international transfer analysis.

expected: Flagged as a conflict. The GDPR guide's scoped wording is what can be sent: region pins the primary database, Auth and Storage, but region choice alone is not a residency guarantee for everything. A commitment request goes to a person.

statement: The 2025 security retro (January 2026) is past its library expiry (2026-07-07); its 'what's next for 2026' list is a dated plan.

evidence.quote: Several security improvements are planned for this year:

expected: Used for what shipped in 2025. Its planned items (paid bounties, push protection, BYOC, grant toggles) are reported as plans of January 2026, never as current capability, and the item is reported as expired.
